title: Executable skills in the coevo5 harness: a GLM-written state-tracker program for ALFWorld, verified by replay, raises training success well above control; SpreadsheetBench programs show little value
verdict_cn:
结论：在"家务文字游戏"（ALFWorld）上，给模型配一个由程序自动运行的"记事小工具"很有希望；在"表格编辑题"（SpreadsheetBench）上目前用处很小，暂不建议投入。
理由：现在的评测程序每一步只让模型看最近5步，它记不住哪些柜子翻过。历史训练数据里，失败局全部是50步用完，约三分之一的步数在重复去看过的地方。上一轮手写的小工具替模型记"去过哪、看到什么、还没去哪、手里拿什么"，42个训练游戏中成功从16个升到28个（纯属偶然的可能性约千分之四）。这一轮让方法里负责分析的模型GLM-5.3只调用一次（约5千个"词元"，即模型计费的字数单位）就写出同功能的工具；不调用解题模型，用228局历史记录共7524步自动回放检查，零错误；实际试玩39局：成功25局，对照组15局（11局变好、1局变差），与手写版的28局差别不显著。
表格题：自动检查能准确找出部分失败，但据此让模型改一次，只比重做一次多救回3题（14比11，不显著）；主要失败是"理解错题意"，工具帮不上。
代价与局限：技能不再只是一段文字，评测程序要升级、所有基线要重跑；这个游戏没有"相似的别的考试"，只能证明本考试内的学习，不能证明跨考试迁移。建议先做一次事先登记的复现（约1400万词元、约8小时，含"安慰剂工具"对照）。
what_i_did:
1. Read the shared context. Read both earlier D3 rounds' leftovers (scripts, logs, pilot outputs on the new machine and the Mac); neither round had written a report.
2. Read the harness code:
   - skillopt/coevo5/cells.py: the cell lifecycle, the remedies (which never replace a delivered answer), and the Skill hash.
   - skillopt/continual_eval/backends.py: the SpreadsheetBench one-shot solve, docker execution and the qualified v7 LibreOffice-recalculation scorer; the ALFWorld per-step loop, whose view carries only recent_history[-5:].
   - native_worker.py: exec() of the delivered program inside a network-less, read-only container.
   - code_delivery.py: strict fence extraction.
   - coevo5/protocol.py: taxonomy, pools, runtime.
   - coevo5/data.py: the training pool is the historical train + val parts, so the alfworld/val:* games are training items.
   - The runtime section of the v3 manifest on the new machine.
3. Checked the earlier rounds' work:
   - Matched the pilot scripts by md5 to the files that ran.
   - Recomputed from raw episode and job files: the ALFWorld tracker pilot B, the SpreadsheetBench repair-vs-resample pilot, and the fence-salvage counts.
   - Reviewed but did not re-run: the reference-free hard-flag detector and the GLM-induced-check pilot.
4. Re-derived the v3 stage-4/5 training failure anatomy myself (r3/v3_facts.py): verdicts, failure kinds, examiner codes, steps, revisits a tracker would flag, unreached receptacles, wrapper actions, tokens per cell and per call. Also measured:
   - v3 ALFWorld reply lengths (18,589 replies);
   - docker generation wall times;
   - v3 pass rates and run-to-run flips on the pilot's 42 games.
5. New pilot:
   - One GLM-5.3 call wrote a Tracker program from a registered interface.
   - I read the code, then verified it by sandboxed replay (network-less, read-only container) over all 228 v3 ALFWorld training traces (7,524 steps), with six property checks and step-by-step agreement against the hand-written tracker.
   - I then ran it in the 42 training games of pilot B, with pilot B's exact loop and settings and only the tracker swapped (6 workers, 1.6M-token cap), and compared against pilot B's arms on the same games. 39 of 42 games were complete at report time.
6. Verified the key literature at abstract/summary level: Voyager, AdaPlanner, ASI, SkillWeaver, StateAct, SpreadsheetBench, and Liu et al. 2026.
7. The harness refused writing report.md for a subagent, so the full report content is in these fields.
evidence:
Labels: MEASURED = computed by me in this round from raw data. RECOMPUTED = an earlier round's pilot, script hash-checked and numbers recomputed from raw records. PRIOR = an earlier round's analysis, logic reviewed but not re-run. All data are training-side.

HARNESS FACTS (from the code)
- SpreadsheetBench, solve:
  - One model call per cell. The system prompt is the contract (contract-first-v2: one ```python program that reads input.xlsx and writes output.xlsx) followed by the Skill text.
  - The user message holds the instruction, a workbook preview (5 rows x 20 columns per sheet), and the answer position.
  - Code extraction is strict: an unclosed fence counts as a 'malformed' failure.
- SpreadsheetBench, execution and scoring:
  - Execution runs in image sha256:0a0a5dcb with --network=none --read-only --user=65534 --cap-drop=ALL --memory=4096m --cpus=1, a 300 s timeout and python -I -B. The worker exec()s the program as __main__.
  - There is no helper path or library field.
  - The scorer is qualified_lo_recalc_v7_v1, with LibreOffice in image sha256:f7f6. Every case must pass.
  - It is a one-shot profile. Remedies never replace a delivered answer, so a repair turn would have to be a new solver profile.
- ALFWorld:
  - One call per step, up to 50 steps.
  - The view is the initial observation, the current observation, the admissible commands and only the last 5 (observation, action) pairs.
  - The action is executed verbatim. The Skill is re-sent every step.

MEASURED, v3 ALFWorld stage-5 training (57 games x 2 runs per chain)
- Pass rates: E-ds 46/114, I-ds 58/114.
- Every failure ends at the 50-step budget: 68/68 and 56/56.
- Go-to steps to an already-reached receptacle, per failing episode: 14.9 (E-ds) and 17.8 (I-ds). Per passing episode: 2.0 and 2.3. These are 1,010/3,400 (29.7%) and 994/2,800 (35.5%) of all failing steps.
- At the end of a failure, 20.2 of 26.1 (E-ds) and 19.7 of 25.9 (I-ds) receptacles were never reached.
- Examiner code D3 'search loop' on 88/124 failures (71%).
- 34/68 E-ds failures contain a wrapper-form action ('action: ...') that was executed verbatim.
- Tokens per call: 820 for E-ds (3,957 calls) vs 3,377 for I-ds (3,567 calls), because the Skill is re-sent every step.
- Over 18,589 stage-5 replies: median 12 completion tokens, p99 336, max 32,768; 106 replies exceeded 512.
- On the pilot's 42 games, v3 passed E-ds 30/84 (35.7%) and I-ds 38/84 (45.2%). 6 of 42 games flip between two identical runs in each chain.

MEASURED, v3 SpreadsheetBench stage-4 training (91 qualified items x 1 run)
- pass/fail/other: E-ds 46/44/1, I-ds 47/43/1.
- Failure codes: D4 'wrong logic' 52/87 (60%); D1+D2+D5+D6 together 25/87 (29%).
- Program defect + truncated + malformed: 7/44 and 7/43.
- Generation container wall time: median 1.34 s, mean 1.65 s, max 26 s (n=176).

MEASURED, new pilot (learned tracker)
- One GLM-5.3 call, 4,986 tokens, first attempt. It produced a 5,087-byte standard-library program (sha256 ed49e788417c35b1...).
- Sandboxed replay took 2.8 s wall. Over 228 traces and 7,524 steps: 0 exceptions, 0 malformed or oversize views, 0 violations across 4,218 arrival/open events and 632 pick-up/place events, and exact rejection counts.
- Agreement with the hand-written tracker: reached/unreached sets identical on 7,350/7,524 steps (97.7%); carrying and rejection counts identical on 7,524/7,524. The divergences come from two defensible choices: whether 'examine X' or 'move obj to X' counts as reaching X.
- Episodes (one run, pilot B's loop and settings, 39 of 42 complete):

| Arm | Passes (39 games) | Tokens per episode | Calls per episode | Revisits per failing episode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-glm (GLM-written tracker) | 25/39 | 30.9k | 25.5 | 8.8 |
| T-hand (hand-written tracker) | 28/39 | 30.2k | 24.8 | 5.6 |
| C (no tracker) | 15/39 | 30.1k | 34.7 | 19.9 |

  - T-glm vs C: 11 games better, 1 worse, exact sign test p=0.0063, paired difference +0.256 [0.100, 0.413].
  - T-hand vs C on the same games: 14 better, 1 worse, p=0.0010.
  - T-glm vs T-hand: 2 vs 5 discordant games, p=0.45, difference -0.077 [-0.209, 0.056].

RECOMPUTED (earlier rounds)
- Pilot B, setup: 42 training games, E-ds empty scaffold, one run per arm. Both arms used max_tokens 512 and the same robust parser; the only difference was the tracker view field.
- Pilot B, results:
  - T 28/42 vs C 16/42: 14 vs 2 discordant, p=0.0042, paired difference +0.286 [0.118, 0.453].
  - By task type (T-only vs C-only games): cool 4/0, heat 3/0, look 3/0, clean 2/1, simple 1/1, two-object 1/0.
- Under the frozen 32,768-token cap (design A), 3 of 4 tracker episodes ended in runaway truncated replies (36k to 50k tokens per episode).
- SpreadsheetBench, repair turn (R) vs plain re-sample (S) on 47 hard-flagged parent failures: R 14/47 vs S 11/47, discordant 8 vs 5, p=0.58. Crashed or malformed programs: 13 vs 8 of 26. Semantic flags: 1 vs 3 of 17.
- Fence salvage: of 91 unclosed-fence 'malformed' failures, lenient extraction scored by the frozen scorer gives 31 pass, 58 fail, 2 unknown.

PRIOR (not re-run)
- Reference-free hard checks fire on 290/780 failures and 0/599 passes over 1,397 v3 sheet cells. Caveat: the answer sheet was resolved against the reference workbook's sheet list.
- GLM-induced checks: 1 of 4 accepted. On the held-out half it flagged 0/134 passes and 2/102 extra failures.
design:
DEFINITION. An executable skill is a program in a typed slot of the frozen harness.
- The protocol registers the slot: inputs (public text only), bounded output, when the harness calls it, time and memory limits, allowed imports.
- The method writes the program body. The harness executes it.
- The Skill identity hash covers text + programs + interface version.
- Each program is at most about 8 KB and sits outside MAX_SKILL_BYTES; only its one-line description counts against the text limit.

SLOTS, in priority order
1. alfworld.observer
   - Interface: Tracker(initial_observation); update(action, observation); view() returning a dict of at most 1,500 characters.
   - The harness adds the view to every step under a fixed key, with one fixed system sentence.
   - Evidence: both tracker pilots.
2. alfworld.actuator
   - Interface: map(reply, admissible), returning an admissible command that the reply names, or the reply unchanged.
   - A hygiene fix: 34/68 E-ds failures executed wrapper-form actions verbatim. Its effect is unmeasured; it could also be a fixed harness fix.
3. spreadsheetbench.library
   - A module written next to input.xlsx inside the existing container and importable by the solver's program. Its API description goes into the Skill text.
   - No evidence yet. It targets D1/D2/D5/D6, 29% of failures.
4. spreadsheetbench.checks + one repair turn
   - Precise but low yield. Better as a fixed solver profile applied to all arms.
5. alfworld.macros
   - Voyager/AdaPlanner-style composite actions. Future work: changes the action interface and step accounting.

VERIFICATION BY EXECUTION, cheapest first
- V0 static: the program parses; an AST whitelist of imports; no I/O, network, eval or exec; a size bound; literals scanned against training gold values, item ids, game files and instance names.
- V1 replay, zero solver tokens: run in a sandbox on stored training traces or input workbooks. Requires no exceptions, identical output over two runs, bounded output, and property checks such as the six used here. Pre-register the thresholds, e.g. 0 exceptions and under 1% violations. Here one container run judged 7,524 steps in 2.8 s.
- V2 selftest on the program's own evidence items.
- V3 the existing screen/confirm, with program placebos as controls: same schema and size, uninformative content (for example 'reached' frozen at the initial state, or permuted receptacle names); a no-op library for SpreadsheetBench.
- V4 test, frozen under the full-identity hash.

HOW THE METHOD PRODUCES PROGRAMS
- A new analyst proposal type, 'program', allowed only for registered slots.
- Its input: the slot interface, one worked example, failures carrying the slot's target codes (ALFWorld D3/D4), and aggregate statistics computed by the harness.
- About 5k GLM tokens per proposal (measured).
- What the method cannot claim: that it discovered the need for the slot. The protocol designer registered it.

PROTOCOL CHANGES, file level
- Skill object (skill.py): add programs. These identities must hash text + programs:
  - cells.py:222 (skill_sha256 of the text);
  - evaluation.py:356/366, which reuses test evaluation when the text digest is unchanged and would wrongly reuse results when only a program changed;
  - step.py:825 and chain.py:290.
- Backends v2:
  - _solve_alfworld calls the sandboxed observer after each env.step.
  - _native and native_worker get a library_source field, written as a module and put on sys.path; the image is unchanged.
  - cells._replay must replay with the same library.
- A repair turn becomes a two-call solver profile with new handling in decision-table rows 5/6/9a/9c.
- An ALFWorld per-step truncation policy for every arm, since the tracker triggered runaway replies under the 32,768 cap.
- leakage.py: a literal scan for code.
- gate.py: a V0/V1 stage and placebo programs.
- Fresh stage-0 baselines under v2 with the slots empty.

pilot.result: (a) Learned tracker, induction plus verification by execution (MEASURED): one GLM-5.3 call (4,986 tokens) wrote a 5,087-byte standard-library program. Sandboxed replay over all 228 v3 ALFWorld training traces (7,524 steps) found 0 exceptions, 0 malformed or oversize views, and 0 property violations (4,218 arrival/open events, 632 pick-up/place events). It agreed with the hand-written tracker on 97.7% of steps. (b) Episodes: pilot B's exact loop and settings with only the tracker swapped; E-ds empty scaffold Skill, deepseek-v4-flash, max_tokens 512, 50 steps, one run; 39 of 42 training games complete at report time. GLM-written tracker 25/39 vs no-tracker control 15/39 on the same games: 11 better, 1 worse, exact sign test p=0.0063, paired difference +0.256 [0.100, 0.413]. Hand-written tracker on the same games: 28/39. GLM vs hand-written: 2 vs 5 discordant, p=0.45, not distinguishable. Tokens per episode: 30.9k vs 30.1k for control. Revisits per failing episode: 8.8 vs 19.9. This is positive, but: no placebo arm; one run; the comparison arms ran 1.5 to 5 hours earlier; and the loop departs from the frozen one (512-token cap, robust parser in all arms).

risks:
1. Credit assignment, the main conceptual risk.
   - A tracker is an agent upgrade. If every arm gets it, the learning question stays text-only. If only the method can fill the slot, a reviewer can say the designer engineered the loop.
   - In this pilot the interface and the idea came from me, with hindsight from the v3 analysis; GLM wrote only the body.
   - Defensible framing: a registered empty slot, filled from failure evidence, verified by execution, that beats both the empty slot and a placebo program. Report the hand-written program as an engineered reference, as the task card is for text.
2. No placebo arm yet, so 'any structured extra field helps' is not excluded.
3. One run per arm. v3 shows 14% of games flip between identical runs, so the confidence intervals are wide.
4. T-glm ran 1.5 to 5 hours after pilot B's arms (possible route or time effects), and 3 of 42 games were unfinished at report time.
5. The pilots changed the loop: a 512-token cap and a robust parser in all arms. Under the frozen 32,768 cap, the tracker arm mostly died of runaway replies (3 of 4 episodes). A v5 truncation policy is a precondition.
6. Measured only with the empty scaffold Skill. With the task-card Skill, which is already about +9.5 points on these games in v3, the gain is unmeasured.
7. ALFWorld programs would run in the host process unless sandboxed.
8. Code can memorize games. Replay verification does not detect overfitting; only held-out gating and the test split do.
9. Benchmark-locality: ALFWorld has no registered similar benchmark, and OfficeQA cannot run code. The current suite cannot show transfer of executable skills.
10. SpreadsheetBench: repair is about equal to a re-sample, induced checks add almost nothing, and wrong logic (D4) dominates. Investment there is speculative.
11. Any backend change starts a new protocol version. v3 stage tables are not comparable without re-run baselines.
cost_estimate:
MEASURED UNIT COSTS
- Tracker induction: 4,986 GLM tokens per proposal.
- Replay verification: 0 tokens, 2.8 s wall.
- ALFWorld episodes with the empty scaffold Skill: about 30k to 31k deepseek tokens each (pilot B mean 31.6k; this round 30.9k), at 6.2 to 9.4 worker-minutes each.
- v3 I-ds calls cost 4.1x E-ds calls (3,377 vs 820 tokens per call) because the Skill is re-sent every step.
- SpreadsheetBench program execution: median 1.34 s.

ESTIMATES
- One ALFWorld program screen on all 57 training games (program arm 2 runs, parent 2 runs, two placebos 1 run each = 342 episodes):
  - about 10.8M tokens with an empty-scaffold Skill, about 40M with a task-card-size Skill;
  - confirm roughly doubles it;
  - 5.9 to 9 h wall per screen at the registered 6 episode slots.
  - It fits the 200M per-chain deepseek cap. Wall time is the binding cost.
- SpreadsheetBench: a library screen is about 3 to 4M tokens. A repair profile adds one call (about 4.4k tokens) per flagged cell, about 14% of parent cells.
- Engineering: ALFWorld observer slot about 2 to 3 days including review and smoke; SpreadsheetBench library slot about 1 to 2 days; repair profile about 2 days.
- Recommended replication: 57 games x 2 runs x 4 arms (C, T-hand, T-glm frozen at sha ed49e788..., T-placebo) = 456 episodes, about 14.4M deepseek tokens, 8 to 12 h on 6 workers.

THIS ROUND'S SPEND: 4,986 GLM tokens + about 1.21M deepseek tokens (39 completed episodes; up to about 0.1M more for the 3 in flight).
recommendation:
1. ALFWorld: do it.
   - Register an alfworld.observer program slot for v5, gated by V0/V1 replay verification and program placebos.
   - Before building the full method path, run one pre-registered replication:
     - 57 training games x 2 runs;
     - arms: C, T-hand, T-glm (frozen now at sha ed49e788...) and T-placebo;
     - primary contrast T-glm vs C, secondary T-glm vs T-placebo;
     - under the v5 per-step truncation policy;
     - repeated once with the task-card Skill.
   - If T-glm beats the placebo, the paper gets a clean result: an execution-verified state abstraction written by the method's own role model.
   - The owner must first choose the credit-assignment framing (risk 1).
2. SpreadsheetBench: do not build executable skills now.
   - Optionally adopt 'reference-free check + one re-sample' as a noise-reducing solver profile for every arm.
   - Separately, decide the unclosed-fence extraction policy as a new protocol version: 31 of 91 strict 'malformed' failures were working programs.
   - Revisit a helper library only if the failure mix moves away from wrong logic (D4).
3. Later: ALFWorld macro-actions, only after the observer result replicates.
4. Cross-references to other directions:
   - D14: the 5-step window is the mechanism behind the text-skill limit on ALFWorld.
   - D5: delivery failures and re-sample rescues are measurement noise.
   - D2: a verified program library is case memory with code.
   - Co-evolution ('coding rubric'): execution-verified checks are a concrete instance; on SpreadsheetBench they were precise but low-yield.
references:
All checked at abstract or summary level (CLAIM).
- Voyager. Wang et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.16291, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291. An executable skill library: a program is added after self-verification using environment feedback and execution errors, and retrieved by embedding. Reports 3.3x more unique items and tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster.
- AdaPlanner. Sun et al., NeurIPS 2023, arXiv 2305.16653, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.16653. Code-style plans refined from feedback; successful plans are reused as examples. About 91.8% on ALFWorld's 134 tasks with text-davinci-002.
- ASI, Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks. Wang, Gandhi, Neubig, Fried, COLM 2025, arXiv 2504.06821, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.06821. Programmatic skills verified by execution: +23.5% success on WebArena over the static agent, +11.3% over its text-skill counterpart.
- SkillWeaver. Zheng et al. 2025, arXiv 2504.07079, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.07079. Synthesized and honed APIs; relative gains of 31.8% on WebArena and 39.8% on real sites.
- StateAct. Rozanov & Rei, REALM 2025, arXiv 2410.02810, https://aclanthology.org/2025.realm-1.27. State tracking (location, inventory) beats ReAct by more than 10% on ALFWorld. This is independent support for the memory bottleneck found here.
- SpreadsheetBench. Ma et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B, arXiv 2406.14991, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14991v2. Multi-round inference with execution-error feedback improves over single-round.
- Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills. Liu et al. 2026, arXiv 2608.02636, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02636. Evolution is sparse: 55 of 388 candidates set a byte-distinct validation best. With GPT-5.5 on SpreadsheetBench, oracle parallel sampling came 30.96 points short of the evolved skill.
- Code: skillopt/coevo5/cells.py, skillopt/continual_eval/backends.py, native_worker.py, code_delivery.py, skillopt/coevo5/protocol.py, skillopt/coevo5/data.py; manifest /data/coevo5-20261019-v3-run-manifest.json (runtime section).
